title.value: Noisy ZSC: Breaking The Common Knowledge Assumption In Zero-Shot Coordination Games

extractions.description: The paper introduces the noisy zero-shot coordination (NZSC) problem setting, in which agents observe different noisy versions of the ground truth Dec-POMDP, shows that NZSC can be reduced to standard ZSC via a meta-Dec-POMDP, proposes toy lever-game environments, and empirically evaluates IPPO with self-play and other-play objectives in them.

type.quote: In our experiments, we analyze various aspects of NZSC and show that achieving good performance in NZSC requires agents to make use of both the noisy observations of ground truth Dec-POMDP
type.justification: The paper formulates a setting and runs experiments with learning agents in toy environments, reporting regret and coordination failure rates.

name.quote: Zero-shot coordination (ZSC) is a popular setting for studying the ability of AI agents to coordinate with novel partners.
name.justification: The paper's central setting, which it extends with NZSC.

name.quote: Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning: A general fully cooperative multi-agent reinforcement learning problem (MARL) with n-agents is represented as a Decentralized Partially Observable Markov Decision Process (Dec-POMDP)
name.justification: The problem is formulated as a cooperative MARL problem and solved with MARL algorithms.
